howDoI.q: How do I make a key my hero carries on to the next level?
How do I make a door that a key from another level will not open?
How do I copy a key and its door onto a counter of their own?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Not That Key is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Keys and doors are counters. Here the counters go with you from level to level, so play the levels in order.

pages.head: Level 1: Take Both Keys
pages.html:
Level 1: Take Both Keys

Two gold keys lie on the ground, and one gold door stands in a wall further on. Take both keys and walk into the door. It opens and takes one key. The other stays with you, and the last sign says so. There are eight coins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The keys. Open notkey.bbl in the blocks editor and pick the key block. On its Touch tab, Effect counter is counter 20 and Effect amount is 1. Touch it and counter 20 goes up by one.
  • The door. The gate block has the same Effect counter, 20, with an Effect amount of −1. It takes one key and no more, so with two keys one is left.
  • The spare. Counters are not reset when a level ends. The next level starts with whatever the counter held. Nothing in this level saves the spare: the engine just carries it.
  • The start. Open hero.chr in the character editor. Counter 20 starts at 1, which the game shows as none carried.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side with the words drawn in their pictures.

pages.head: Level 2: The Spare Fits
pages.html:
Level 2: The Spare Fits

A gold door stands near the start, and there is no key in front of it. Walk into it: the spare from level 1 opens it. Behind the door lies one more gold key, and you take it, so you leave with a spare again. There are ten coins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The same door. Open two.map in the map editor. The door is the same gate block as level 1, so it still wants counter 20. Nothing in this level mentions level 1.
  • Why it opens. Counter 20 still holds the spare. The touch can be paid for, so the door takes one and becomes sky.
  • The new key. It is the same key block, placed after the door. A level a player starts by itself, without level 1 before it, starts with no key, so this door stays shut. The level is made to be played in order.

pages.head: Level 3: Not That Key
pages.html:
Level 3: Not That Key

A blue door with a green padlock stands in a wall, and you reach it holding a gold key. Walk into it: nothing happens, and you keep the key. The A GOLD KEY IS NOT A GREEN KEY sign says why. Climb the ladder to the ledge for the green key, come down and walk into the door. It opens. A gold door farther on takes the gold key you carried all along. There are eight coins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • A set copied onto another counter. Open three.bbl and compare key, gate and gateTop with keyGreen, gateGreen and gateTopGreen. They are copies. Only the picture and the Effect counter differ: counter 22 instead of 20. Counter 21 is left unused. Any number from 20 to 29 works.
  • A copy of the set for this level. Levels 1 and 2 load notkey.bbl. Level 3 loads three.bbl, a copy of it with the green set added after the last shared block, so every shared block keeps its number. Open notkey.gam in the scenes editor and look at the block set each scene loads. Only level 3 needs the green blocks, so the others never carry them.
  • Why the gold key fails. The green door takes from counter 22. That counter holds nothing, so the touch cannot be paid for and the door stays shut. Counter 20, with the gold key in it, is a different counter.
  • Counters are numbers. A counter has no name. Gold and green are only the colors in the pictures. The key, the door and the sign agree because you made them agree.
  • The start. Open hero.chr in the character editor. Counter 22 starts at 1, like counter 20.
  • The gold door. It is the level 1 gate again. It takes the gold key you carried through two levels.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

A key here is a counter, and that is all it is:

  • Counters have numbers, not names. The editor shows counter 22, never “green”. Nothing stops a door and a key from using different numbers by mistake, so keep a list of which number is which.
  • There are ten counters for keys and the like, numbers 20 to 29. Past that, a copy of the set has no number to use.
  • Counters carry from level to level and cannot be given a level of their own. A different number for each level's keys is how to keep them apart.
  • A copy of the block set is a whole file. Change a shared block in one copy and the others do not follow, so change shared blocks in every copy.
  • Nothing shows a number. The game shows no key counts, so the player learns what they carry by trying doors.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In notkey.bbl, change gateGreen's Effect counter to 20. Now the gold key opens the green door, and the green key is no use.
  • Change keyGreen's counter to 20 as well. Both colors now add to the same counter.
  • Copy key, gate and gateTop again, set them to counter 23 and draw them blue. You have a third kind of key.
  • Raise gate's Effect amount to −2. Now the spare is not enough on its own.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.tagline: A gold key will not open a green door.
box.back: A small explorer in a gold beanie keeps a spare key from one level to the next, until a green door will not take it. Counters carry across levels and have numbers, not names, so each door answers only to its own. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and copy a key and a door onto a counter of your own.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
A spare key goes with you to the next level
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Three short levels about keys that travel. A key you do not use stays in your pocket when the level ends, so a spare opens a door two levels later. But a green door has its own counter, and a gold key will not open it. Signs in the levels say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and give a door a counter of its own.

57.long: Jump. Steer with Left and Right while you are in the air.

counters.20: Gold keys carried. They carry on to the next level.
counters.22: Green keys carried: a green key adds one, a green door takes one.
